method: Canvas resolution is the tile resolution multiplied by the grid: canvas width = tile width x tiles across and canvas height = tile height x tiles down. One tile's physical size follows from its diagonal d and aspect ratio a = tile width / tile height, with tile height = d / sqrt(a^2 + 1) and tile width = tile height x a, using 25.4 mm per inch. The wall adds one bezel between neighbouring tiles: wall width = tiles across x tile width + (tiles across - 1) x vertical bezel, and likewise for height. Pixel pitch is tile width in millimetres divided by tile width in pixels; pixel density is canvas width divided by the wall width in inches; bezel share is the total seam width (or height) divided by the wall width (or height) and is reported as zero when there is only one tile in that direction. Aspect ratios are reduced by their greatest common divisor. The model assumes identical tiles at their native resolution, uniform bezels, no mounting gaps, no processor scaling and no bezel compensation, and it does not cover viewing distance, brightness, mounting structure or signal routing. Inputs are limited to tiles of 64-16384 px, grids of 1-32 per direction, diagonals of 5-300 in and bezels of 0-200 mm. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
